sections.h2: Where the Erie County recorder is and what it handles
sections.html:
The Erie County Recorder's Office is in the Erie County Office Building at 247 Columbus Avenue, Suite 225, Sandusky, OH 44870, phone (419) 627-7686. The counter is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. and closes for the usual holidays, including Juneteenth, Columbus Day and the day after Thanksgiving. When a holiday lands on a Saturday the office closes the Friday before, and a Sunday holiday means closing the Monday after.

The office records deeds, mortgages, releases and similar papers, and it also takes military discharges. It is not a place to get paperwork drafted. Staff are not attorneys, keep no forms, run no lien or title searches, and cannot advise on how to prepare a legal document.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Erie County?
sections.html:
Recording costs the same in every Ohio county and is charged by page: $34 total for the first two printed pages, then $8 for each page after that. A sheet printed on both sides counts as two pages. A two-page document costs $34 and a three-page one $42.

Type of chargeAmount
First two printed pages$34 total
Each page after the first two$8
Marginal reference, such as an assignment or release$4 per document reference
Affidavit for transfer (successor trustee)No $4 marginal fee
Document that fails Ohio Revised Code standards$20 nonconformance fee
Copies not available free online$2 per page

Copy requests paid by card over the phone carry a processor charge, a $2 minimum and up to 2 or 3 percent of the total, and American Express is not taken. Every charge in the office is fixed by the Ohio Revised Code, so staff cannot waive or negotiate them.

sections.h2: What an Erie County deed must contain
sections.html:
The office publishes Basic Recording Requirements that spell out what gets a document turned away. Originals must be legible with original signatures, and photocopies are refused. Staff check a long list before they stamp anything.

  • A full legal description beginning "Situated in" the city or township, county and state, not the short description from the auditor's site or a tax bill.
  • A printed or typed name under every signature, and a full notary clause with the notary's stamp or printed name and the commission expiration date.
  • Both a first and last name for every party, with marital status. The office recommends that the spouse of a married grantor sign and be notarized, even only to release dower.
  • A "Prepared By" line naming whoever drafted the document, and every attached exhibit that the document mentions.
  • No Social Security numbers or tax ID numbers. The office redacts the number on an original death certificate itself, and the certificate must stay unmarked.
  • For a signer acting under a power of attorney, the Erie County recording number of the power, or the power recorded just ahead of the deed in the same package.

White-out is not allowed. The $20 nonconformance fee applies when a document misses these standards, which is why staff suggest stopping in first so they can look it over.

sections.h2: Can I mail a deed or record it electronically?
sections.html:
A deed that transfers property cannot be mailed. Any document that transfers property, or a transfer on death designation or confirmation, must be stamped by the Transfer office and then carried in or recorded electronically, never sent by mail, UPS or FedEx. The office can e-record almost every document type, transfer deeds included, for filers with an account at one of its listed vendors: ePN-eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile or CSC.

Papers that do not need the Transfer stamp can come by mail with a self-addressed stamped envelope large enough for everything. Each document goes through recording, indexing and verification before it is mailed back, and the usual turnaround is one to two business days before it goes out in the mail.

sections.h2: Conveyance and transfer fees on an Erie County sale
sections.html:
The county auditor sets the conveyance fee at $4.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price, charged on real estate and on manufactured homes. A separate transfer fee is $0.50 per line. The rate history runs from $1 per $1,000 in May 1969 to March 1990, rising in steps to $4 per $1,000 since February 1994.

An exemption has to meet a qualification on the state's DTE 100EX form, and the auditor's site has a Conveyance Fee Calculator that asks for the number of properties and the sale amount. The auditor's office is at 247 Columbus Avenue, Room 210, phone (419) 627-7746. Ask the recorder's staff where to get the Transfer stamp before you walk a deed to Suite 225.

sections.h2: Finding a recorded deed or a mortgage release
sections.html:
Start with the free online search at the county's self-service site. Indexing and images go back to 1990, with older documents being added, and you can download or print images for free. Enter the last name first, then the first name, such as Smith Jane, in the Both Names box.

Two points help sellers. The recorder does not hold your deed: you receive the original recorded deed at purchase, and the office keeps copies only. A paid-off mortgage produces a separate release or satisfaction, so a seller who cannot find proof of a payoff should look for that recorded document.

sections.h2: Erie County property tax and your deed
sections.html:
The county bills a year behind, and taxes follow the property, not the owner, so the balance on a parcel matters at closing. Real estate bills for 2027 are due February 19 and July 16. The treasurer's office is at 247 Columbus Avenue, Suite 115, phone (419) 627-7701.

The treasurer sorts the county's school districts by whether parcels may get the Inflation Cap Credit created by House Bill 186.

  • May receive it: Bellevue, Edison, Firelands, Huron, Monroeville, Vermilion and Western Reserve.
  • Will not receive it: Kelleys Island, Margaretta, Perkins and Sandusky.
  • Homestead: the auditor lists a $40,000 household income threshold for applicants who are 65 or older or disabled.
  • Overdue parcels: sold only at sheriff's sale.

Erie County sits on the Lake Erie shore, and 374 of its 626 square miles are water, which leaves 252 square miles of land. Sandusky is the seat and largest city. The 2025 estimate is 73,296 people, down 3.1% from 2020, and owners occupy 71.9% of homes. A typical owner-occupied home is worth $199,700, and median gross rent is $933. Price a particular house with a written offer or a local appraisal instead of a countywide number.

Before you record, check the legal description, find your mortgage release, and decide whether you will walk the deed in or e-record it through a title company. A cash buyer does not change those steps.

faqs.q: How much does the Erie County recorder charge for a two-page deed?
faqs.a: The charge is $34 for the first two printed pages. Each further page costs $8, and a document printed on both sides of one sheet counts as two pages.

faqs.q: Can I mail an Erie County deed to the recorder?
faqs.a: No, not if it transfers property. Those documents must be stamped by the Transfer office and delivered in person or recorded electronically through a listed vendor.

faqs.q: What is the Erie County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The auditor charges $4.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price, plus a $0.50 per line transfer fee. Call the auditor at (419) 627-7746 to confirm figures for your closing.

faqs.q: Does the Erie County recorder keep my original deed?
faqs.a: No. The recorder keeps copies only, and you receive the original recorded deed when you buy. A mortgage payoff produces its own release document.

faqs.q: What time does the Erie County recorder open and close?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Closed days include Juneteenth, Columbus Day, Thanksgiving, the day after Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
